newsitem.title: FRANCE: Voting starts in French cliffhanger election.
newsitem.headline: Voting starts in French cliffhanger election.

text.p: Voting began in France on Sunday in the cliffhanger final round of a parliamentary election in which President Jacques Chirac is gambling on winning a renewed centre-right majority.
Polling stations opened at 8 a.m. (0600 GMT) in mainland France and are due to close at 8 p.m. (1800 GMT).

Some 39 million voters are due to choose 577 National Assembly deputies. The weather was sunny in most of France but rain was expected across the south of the country. First result projections are due immediately after the close of polling.
The Socialist-Communist camp scored an upset win in the first round of the election a week ago and Chirac has tried to salvage the hopes of the centre-right by ditching Prime Minister Alain Juppe.

Chirac has launched a "dream ticket" made up of socially-conscious Philippe Seguin, tipped for the job of prime minister if the centre-right wins, and free-marketeer Alain Madelin, a likely finance minister.

Both camps say the outcome is likely to be tight. Chirac risks his presidency with the snap election. If his ruling coalition loses, he will be forced into an uneasy "cohabitation", or power-sharing, with a government led by Socialist leader Lionel Jospin.
